header.name: Quantum Communication and Networks
header.description: Traditionally, security to information exchange over classical communication channels has been provided by computationally complex encryption algorithms. However, given the anticipated research and development in Quantum Computers, these algorithms are at risk of being broken. Additionally, the volume of data has been exponentially rising with the introduction of new telecom services like 5G and IoT, where any compromise in the security of the ICT infrastructure will lead to a high amount of Service Level Agreements (SLA) violations, a deficit of trust and loss of valuable data. Considering these developments, there have been major efforts in developing ICT infrastructure that provides unconditional security while utilizing the fundamental laws of Quantum Mechanics. In this course, the students will be able to appreciate the aspects of Quantum Information while developing an understanding of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols which will form the basis of secured communication in the future. Further students will also learn how to apply QKD in traditional telecom infrastructure (over both fiber and wireless channels) and develop an understanding of Quantum Internet.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can understand basics of Quantum Information Processing

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students can explain the Quantum Detection Theory Fundamentals

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to design Discrete Variable Protocols, Measurement Device Independent Protocols and Continuous Variable Protocols

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will gain exposure to Quantum Networks and their integration with ICT fiber and satellite infrastructure.

lecture_topics: Review of Classical Information theory fundamentals

Quantum Information Processing Fundamentals: State Vectors, Spin 1/2 systems, Hadamard gate, Density operators, Measurements and Uncertainity principle, Superposition Principle, no cloning theorm, Quantum Entanglement basics

Quantum Detection Theory Fundamentals: Binary Quantum Detection, Coherent States, quadrature operators, classical and quantum photon counting receiver, Noise representation, Binary Quantum Detection in the presence of noise, Gaussian and Squeezed states, Gaussian State Detection, Generation of Quantum States and Multilevel Quantum Optical Communications.
Discrete Variable QKD Protocols for secured key exchange
Study of Continous Variable Protocols with secured key exchange.
Quantum Internet over terrestrial networks: Integration of QKD over classical telecom fiber networks
Quantum Internet over Satellite: Tracking and Acquisition, constellation optimisation with LEO and GEO satellites.
